gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the 1,920 Wh ALLPOWERS R2500 V2 that ChatGPT showed as a card is a different generation from the 2,016 Wh R2500 Plus. On ALLPOWERS' US store, B1000/B3000 expansion batteries and 4,000 W parallel output are listed only on the R2500 Plus listings, which are not available. Every R2500 V2 listing (station and kits) gives one XT60 solar input of up to 1,000 W and names no expansion battery.
standout_why: I compared against StormWatts (cited) and Eco Solar Kits (cited); OutageReady and our own page returned an SSL error and could not be read. StormWatts already has the strongest compatibility content. It has the Elite 200 V2 input (12–60 V, 20 A, 1,000 W) and works out that 2× SP200L must be wired in series, because parallel puts about 21.6 A on a 20 A input. It also has the Jackery 2000 v2's 400 W cap over 2× DC8020 and the DELTA 3 Max's single XT60i at 500 W with 2× 220 W in series. Neither page mentions the ALLPOWERS R2500 V2 at all, so neither has its solar-input cap, its connector or the V2/Plus generation split. Eco Solar Kits says the Elite 200 V2 expands with B80/B230/B300, but BLUETTI's own US kit page and support page only list that as an FAQ question, with no answer shown.
decides: On today's 'Kits we link' table, the ≥2,000 W kits that ship now are the R2500 V2 + SP037 400 W (link price $913.49) and the S2000 Pro kits. Every Elite 200 V2 kit is a pre-order dispatching Nov 26 or Dec 25, 2026. That makes the R2500 V2 + SP037 the likely ship-now pick, and this finding supports it with two points. Its XT60 input takes up to 1,000 W, so the 400 W panel uses 40% of it and leaves room for more panels. And the buyer should not expect to add an expansion battery or parallel a second unit, because ALLPOWERS lists those only for the older R2500 Plus. A shopper who wants to add a battery later is better served by a kit whose maker lists expansion. Neither the Elite 200 V2's nor the R2500 V2's maker page confirms expansion today.

findings.label: Solar input on the 600 W kit listing
findings.value: Up to 1,000 W through one XT60 port; takes AC + solar dual input
findings.source_title: ALLPOWERS R2500 V2 + 600W Solar Panel | 2500W Solar Generator Kit
findings.note: From the listing text on the maker's US store, read with storecheck.py search. The text says: 'Maximum 1000W solar input via XT60 port; Supports AC charging, solar charging and AC + solar dual input'. Arithmetic: the 600 W panel uses 60% of the cap and the 400 W SP037 kit uses 40%.

findings.label: Expansion and parallel output listed for the older generation
findings.value: 2,016 Wh; 'Expandable up to 20kWh with B3000 expansion battery' / 'Expandable with B1000'; 'Maximum 4000W AC output with parallel connection'; marked unavailable
findings.source_title: ALLPOWERS R2500 Plus + 400W Solar Panel | 2500W Solar Generator Kit
findings.note: The US store returned available=false for this listing, for the R2500 Plus station (https://iallpowers.com/products/allpowers-r2500-portable-home-backup-power-station-2500w-2016wh) and for the R2500 Plus + 200 W kit. The R2500 V2 station listing and its 100/200/400/600 W kit listings name no expansion battery and no parallel output. The R2500 manual on manuals.plus (2,016 Wh model) also says B1000 expansion takes it to 5,472 Wh, which matches this being a Plus/V1 feature.

Whether the Elite 200 V2 takes an expansion battery (B80/B230/B300/B300K). BLUETTI's US kit page and support page list the FAQ question but show no answer. The Elite 200 V2 manual PDF downloaded but I could not extract its text (local PDF tools needed approval).
